subject: Reservation gating & SLO alignment for ACME dedicated pilot
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Pat Chen <pat@acme.ai>
Cc: procurement@acme.ai
Date: Sat, 7 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Reservation gating & SLO alignment for ACME dedicated pilot

Team / Pat —

Quick context: ACME is planning a 12-week dedicated pilot starting the first week of January. They want a guaranteed lane (reserved capacity) for inference during US business hours for two mid-size models (approx. 1.5–2k tokens/session typical). Procurement asked for clear gating rules, SLOs we can commit to for the pilot, and a proposal for how we handle autoscale exceptions if they need bursts.

Attached are two docs: reservation_matrix_q4.xlsx (requested slot-by-week matrix + expected QPS) and slo-proposal-v1.pdf (initial SLO language). High-level asks from ACME:
- Guaranteed baseline of 10 concurrent inference slots during 9am–6pm PT Mon–Fri.
- Ability to burst up to 25 concurrent for scheduled demos (prebooked 48h notice).
- 99.5% availability on reserved lane during baseline hours, with latency P95 <= 300ms for model-v1.

Can we confirm the following by EOD Monday:
1) Is the baseline/burst ask feasible within the Dedicated reservation framework (Dev + Marcus)?
2) What operational gating should we include so we don't block other enterprise reservations (Marcus + Laura)? Examples: advance-payment window, hard quota breach triggers, automatic fallback to compatible model variant.
3) If we accept burst exceptions, what will we bill? Do we require a temporary capacity top-up purchase or bill on usage? (Laura)

Pat — feel free to chime in if any of this is inaccurate from ACME's side. Once we align internally I can send the formal ask to procurement and get a signed reservation.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Sr. Account Exec, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Pat Chen <pat@acme.ai>
Date: Sun, 8 Nov 2026 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Reservation gating & SLO alignment for ACME dedicated pilot

Kimberly —

Thanks for the summary and the files. Quick technical read and some clarifying questions before we lock SLO wording:

- Workload profile: the XLSX lists peak sessions at 2k tokens/session and ~18 requests/sec during marketing demo windows. Can you confirm whether the 2 models are identical size/architecture or if one is a larger encoder-decoder? Kernel selection and memory layout will differ.

- KV-cache behavior: If sessions are long-lived (multiple sequential calls per session), we should reserve additional ephemeral memory per concurrent slot. If ACME expects many short independent calls rather than long sessions, we can optimize batching differently. Please ask them to list expected session length (avg. turns).

- Autoscale exceptions: we can implement a policy that allows bursts up to an agreed ceiling (25), but enforce a 48h prebook and a hard global cap to avoid jeopardizing other commitments. Operationally we have two options:
  * Temporary top-up (provision extra GPUs into ACME's dedicated pool for the booked window) — simplest for latency guarantees, billed as a pro-rata reserved charge.
  * Soft-burst onto shared spare capacity — cheaper but we drop availability SLAs and traffic may be routed to slightly lower-tier quantized variants.

If ACME requires P95 <= 300ms for model-v1, I recommend top-up for demos. Else we can accept softer latency for bursts and include fallback model variant in the SLO doc.

I can sketch the gating controls: advance-pay requirement for any reserved top-up, automated alerts at 80/90% baseline utilization that trigger ops review, and an emergency throttle if global GPU scarcity is detected.

Happy to join a sync with ACME next week to confirm profile.

—Dev
Principal Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Reservation gating & SLO alignment for ACME dedicated pilot

Kim / Dev / Laura —

From an ops and capacity budgeting perspective: the baseline of 10 reserved slots during business hours for 12 weeks is doable but we should carve it into a specific lane with a hard isolation boundary in the Dedicated fabric. Two practical notes:

1) Finance & procurement: we need a minimum 30-day prepayment for any reserved capacity to protect against churn. If ACME prefers monthly billing we can do it but require a 1.25x safety multiplier on the initial estimate for the first month.

2) Gating rules proposal:
   - Default: baseline reserved lane (10 slots) with SLA of 99.5% availability during baseline hours.
   - Burst path: up to 25 concurrent for prebooked events (48h notice) via temporary top-up. Top-up billed as a pro-rated reserved charge (by GPU-hour) and requires payment confirmation 24h before the event.
   - Fallback: if capacity is constrained and top-up can't be provisioned, traffic will fall back to a quantized model variant with a clearly documented latency variance; customer must sign acceptance.

3) Tickets/automation: We should add an automated reservation ticket workflow (HubSpot -> internal ops ticket) that captures prebook windows and auto-checks capacity pools. I can draft the runbook steps if we get sign-off.

Action items:
- Kimberly: share ACME's confirmed session profile (avg session length, qps) so Dev can finalize memory/kv sizing.
- Kimberly + Procurement: confirm payment term preference so Finance can price the pro-rate.
- Laura: once we have payment terms, can you validate the SLA language in slo-proposal-v1.pdf and confirm whether legal needs changes?

I'll draft the gating policy and send a short runbook for review by EOD Tuesday.

—Marcus
Head of Capacity Planning
Redwood Inference

Thanks all — this is exactly the level of detail I needed. Pat has confirmed via separate note: the two models are different families (one decoder-only, one seq2seq) and average session length is ~6 turns (roughly 900 tokens total). ACME is amenable to the 48h prebook for demos and prefers the temporary top-up approach for latency-sensitive events.

Next steps (agreed):
- Dev: please produce a short tech note by Friday that lists memory overhead per slot for both model families and the recommended GPU types for the top-up.
- Marcus: draft the reservation gating policy and the automated ticket checklist (include the 30-day prepayment option and the 1.25x temporary safety multiplier alternative).
- Laura: review SLO language and confirm legal checkbox; if okay please attach a marked-up PDF and I'll send to ACME procurement.
- Kimberly (me): I'll schedule a 30-minute sync with ACME and ops for next Wed 11/17 at 10am PT and share the DocuSign link for a slot hold once we get the pricing confirmed.

I updated the HubSpot deal with the proposed terms: https://hubspot.com/deal/ACME-Q4-Dedicated-42 and attached the current SLO proposal and reservation matrix. DocuSign link is staged: https://docusign.net/ACME-reservation-2026 — I'll send to procurement after Laura's markup.

Pat — thanks for the quick clarifications. If anything changes on your side about demo frequency please flag.

Best,
